name: Leaderboards
tagline: An ordered list of two or more identified users or groups, ranked together against a shared performance metric and visible as a set.
desc: A leaderboard shows more than one identified entity in the same ranked view, ordered against each other by a shared metric. What separates it from a single stated position is the comparison set itself: other identified users or groups sit alongside the viewer's own placement, browsable by looking at the row above and below it, rather than a number reported on its own. A ranked list counts as a leaderboard whether it spans the whole population or a segment, whether it resets on a schedule or accumulates for the life of the account, and whether every position is shown or only a bounded slice around the top or the viewer.
principle: Seeing named others ordered in the same view turns private effort into a public, browsable contest.
warn: A leaderboard that only shows the very top of a large population demotivates everyone below it by making the visible gap feel insurmountable; a segmented or local view keeps the gap closable for a median user.
variants: Individual leaderboard, ranks single users against each other
Group leaderboard, ranks teams, clans, or leagues as the ranked unit instead of individuals
Periodic leaderboard, resets on a fixed cadence rather than accumulating for the life of the account
Promotion-and-relegation leaderboard, movement between separate ranked tiers replaces one continuous list
Segmented leaderboard, the comparison set is narrowed by geography, friends, or category rather than spanning the whole population
lifecycle: Mid-to-late lifecycle. Strongest once the user has logged enough activity to have a position worth watching move.
